eviction_policies.page_note: There is no radix_cache.mdx in docs/docs/advanced_features (404); the eviction-policy page is radix_eviction_policy.mdx. Its 'Use when' column is the verbatim sentence set requested.

lfu.when_to_use_verbatim: "A small set of prompts is reused far more than the rest, and you want those to survive bursts of one-off traffic."
lfu.evicts_first_verbatim: "The prefix with the fewest cache hits, then the least recent."

tlru.when_to_use_verbatim: "Agentic / multi-turn workloads where tail TTFT matters more than raw hit rate."
tlru.evicts_first_verbatim: "The tail of a conversation beyond what its next prefill needs to meet the TTFT budget (\"TEL-safe\" tokens), then the least recent."
tlru.constraint_verbatim: "Requires the unified radix cache (the default tree)."

priority.when_to_use_verbatim: "You run [priority scheduling](/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments) and want cache retention to follow the same ranking as admission."
priority.evicts_first_verbatim: "The prefix belonging to the lowest-priority request, then the least recent."
priority.caveat_verbatim: "Without priority scheduling every node is priority `0` and this policy is equivalent to `lru`."

eviction_policies.hybrid_mamba_documented_usability: no authoritative source found. No policy row, and no other page in the docs export, states that lfu/tlru/priority work with a hybrid/mamba model. The only adjacent evidence: tlru "Requires the unified radix cache (the default tree)", and session_radix_cache.mdx documents that UnifiedRadixCache has a Mamba component with its own eviction order — "Mamba | The reusable state on the registered leaf | Two LRU passes: unreferenced nodes first, then referenced nodes if more space is required". That row describes the SESSION-aware order over Mamba, not what lfu/tlru/priority do to Mamba state; do not read it as a compatibility guarantee.
eviction_policies.also_verbatim: "All of them fall back to least-recently-used order within a tie."; "A policy only scores. It does not decide how much to free, and it cannot pin KV in memory".

max_mamba_cache_size_semantics.verdict: SLOTS, not tokens. A request's cost is S state slots, and S depends on --mamba-radix-cache-strategy.
max_mamba_cache_size_semantics.documented_default: --max-mamba-cache-size default `None`; argument-table description is only "The maximum size of the mamba cache." (too thin to settle it — the slot semantics come from the pages below).

primary_slot_evidence.quote: "--max-mamba-cache-size = target_concurrency x S is the equivalent explicit pin and overrides the ratio; the calculator emits it alongside."
Low Latency's --max-mamba-cache-size 80 is exactly its 16 concurrent requests × 5 slots.

"extra_buffer supports overlap schedule by allocating extra mamba state buffers to track mamba state for caching (mamba state usage per running req becomes `2x` for non-spec; `1+(1/(2+speculative_num_draft_tokens))x` for spec dec (e.g. 1.16x if speculative_num_draft_tokens==4))"

slots_per_request_per_strategy.extra_buffer: 5 (default where the model's `auto` resolves to extra_buffer; "this model's auto" wording in the Qwen3.8-2.4T page), 4 where PP disables the overlap scheduler
slots_per_request_per_strategy.extra_buffer_lazy: 4 ("lowers extra_buffer's slot cost by allocating one track slot per request instead of two")
slots_per_request_per_strategy.no_buffer: 3 ("The resolver forces --mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer (3 slots per request, overlap scheduler off)")
slots_per_request_per_strategy.verbatim_table_row: "S — KDA state slots per request: extra_buffer=5, extra_buffer_lazy=4, no_buffer=3, disabled radix cache =1. SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK frees one slot on the extra-buffer strategies; with the overlap scheduler off (or pp > 1, which disables it) the track buffer costs one slot instead of two." (Kimi-K3 page, local mirror line 34293)
slots_per_request_per_strategy.spec: speculation adds verify intermediates D, which the engine sizes in a separate buffer and explicitly does NOT fold into the pin: "D is not a term here: the engine divides the state pool by S alone and sizes the speculative verify buffer separately, so folding D into the pin would over-provision the pool."

max_mamba_cache_size_semantics.cookbook_5_slots_per_request_claim: VERIFIED, with scope. '5 state slots per request' is what the docs state for extra_buffer on hybrid GDN/KDA models (three independent cookbook pages: Kimi-K3 line 34293, Qwen3.8 line 47955 table 'extra_buffer (this model's auto) | 5, or 4 where PP disables the overlap scheduler', Qwen3.8-Flash-Next line 48735 "5 with the default exact extra_buffer radix strategy, 4 with extra_buffer_lazy"). It is NOT a universal constant: it is 3 for no_buffer, 1 with radix cache off, and the server_arguments page says `auto` "currently defaults to `no_buffer`" — so 5 applies only where auto resolves to extra_buffer for that model.
max_mamba_cache_size_semantics.clamp_mechanism_verbatim: "So --max-mamba-cache-size has to match the ratio in force, or it silently clamps max_running_requests to a fraction of the target" and "the scheduler caps --max-running-requests to what the mamba pool admits; read the effective value from the startup log, not from /get_server_info."

recommended_value_for_our_box.inputs: declared live: max_mamba_cache_size 64, mamba_full_memory_ratio 0.9 (ratio default 0.9 is now confirmed by the argument table: "The ratio of mamba state memory to full kv cache memory", default `0.9`), --max-running-requests 5
recommended_value_for_our_box.arithmetic: 5 requests x 5 slots (extra_buffer) = 25 slots; x 4 (extra_buffer_lazy) = 20; x 3 (no_buffer) = 15
recommended_value_for_our_box.recommendation: Pin 25 (30 for one request of headroom) rather than 64, AFTER confirming from the boot log which strategy `auto` resolved to. 64 admits 64/S = 12 requests at S=5, i.e. it is NOT binding at --max-running-requests 5 and is over-provisioned by ~39 slots; the docs state the trade is one-for-one with the KV pool ("It will decrease KV cache space as a trade-off"), so those 39 slots are KV tokens we are not using.
recommended_value_for_our_box.consequence_for_the_16pct_window: This REFUTES the R2-A2 hypothesis that 64 slots (~12 requests) is the clamp on the 15.9-16.5% resident window: at max-running-requests 5 the slot budget is satisfied (25 <= 64), so the resident window is a KV-pool / concurrency-of-5 effect, not a slot ceiling. Raising max-mamba-cache-size cannot lift it; lowering it to ~25 returns memory to the KV pool.
recommended_value_for_our_box.caveat: If our model instead resolves to no_buffer (3 slots) or extra_buffer_lazy (4), the pin math changes to 15 or 20; and if max-running-requests is not actually honoured above 5 the strategy must be re-read from the startup log, per the doc quote above.
